Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Steam destinations for Room recovery

2 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

Room can now use the Steam gameplay backend with an ENet or WebSocket coordinator. It retains the same lease, complete-checkpoint and authority-fencing rules. Steam is native-only; Web builds still require RTC gameplay.

Initialize and retain a Steam_Runtime, then select session.backend = .Steam and set session.steam.runtime plus its virtual port. Room derives its registration endpoint from the runtime's actual Steam ID. A supplied registration endpoint must match; a peer for another Steam ID cannot become the approved local authority.

Odin
// runtime was initialized explicitly and will outlive room.
options := room_options_from_your_admission_service
options.session.backend = .Steam
options.session.steam = STEAM_CONFIG
options.session.steam.runtime = &runtime
options.session.steam.virtual_port = 0
// Room supplies this endpoint for process registration. Provisioning can use
// the same helper when initially enrolling this member.
options.registration_endpoint, _ = steam_endpoint(runtime.steam_id, 0)
err := room_open(&room, initial, model, options)

steam_endpoint(id, virtual_port) produces a value-owned coordinator endpoint with host text steam:<decimal-id>:<decimal-virtual-port> and sentinel port 1. The format is explicit and canonical, supports the full nonzero u64 ID and u16 port range including port zero, and does not reinterpret existing ENet/RTC endpoints. The coordinator's authenticated grant is the only source of a remote host ID. Room applies it at initial admission, redirect, takeover and old-host return; published restore uses the same validated transport configuration.

Each connection needs a fresh SteamMultiplayerPeer. Room rejects a one-off Steam_Config.peer because its caller ownership cannot safely span later recovery. Normally the adapter creates the engine peer itself. Applications with custom bindings can set peer_factory(user) -> gd.Variant: return an owned Variant holding a newly created peer. The adapter retains the peer and destroys the returned Variant on every success/failure path. The factory user and runtime must outlive Room. Session retains those factory settings but never retains a borrowed one-off peer in its saved options.

A room uses one gameplay backend. Provision all Steam-host candidates with this Steam endpoint format; this does not implement mixed Steam/ENet/RTC participants in one room. A granted endpoint in another format is refused rather than guessed.

The endpoint selects transport; it does not grant game membership or successor permission. Provisioning must still bind the enrolled token/identity, and only explicitly trusted members may receive complete authority archives. Native Party can use steam_endpoint for its configured admission endpoint and pass Steam Session options into the ordinary Room setup.

The local API-contract fixture validates lifecycle wiring, not Valve networking. Live multi-account Steam acceptance, lobby/invite integration, SteamGameServer support and broader deployment/platform coverage remain open roadmap requirements.
